long_biography.plain_text:
Grupo México was already a major family mining platform when Germán Larrea Mota-Velasco took its reins in 1994. He did not create the original fortune, but he substantially enlarged the business. The acquisition of Asarco deepened its North American copper interests, while investment in freight rail and infrastructure broadened the group beyond mining.

Larrea remains chairman, president and chief executive, combining inherited control with long-term operating leadership. He holds a personal shareholding alongside a larger stake held through the family's holding company. Those positions underpin his wealth, but they are not interchangeable with the conglomerate's market capitalisation, mines, rail network or divisional revenues. His record is therefore best understood as inherited ownership followed by executive expansion, with metals and mining still the core of the enterprise.
